rules: When mstateen0 .CTR is 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, an attempt to access sctrctl, vsctrctl, sctrdepth, or sctrstatus raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, an attempt to access sireg* when siselect is in the range 0x200 through 0x2FF raises an illegal-instruction exception.

When mstateen0 .CTR is 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, an attempt to access vsireg* when vsiselect is in the range 0x200 through 0x2FF raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, execution of the SCTRCLR instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When hstateen0 .CTR is 0, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state (sctrctl, sctrstatus, sireg* (vsireg*)) raise a virtual-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 1 and hstateen0 .CTR is 1, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state behave as described in Section 7.2 and Section 11.2.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 1 and hstateen0 .CTR is 0, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state and VSmode execution of SCTRCLR raise a virtual-instruction exception.
When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and menvcfg .CDE = 0, an attempt to access any sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and menvcfg .CDE = 0, an attempt to access sireg3 or sireg6 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and menvcfg .CDE = 0, an attempt to access sireg4 or sireg5 when XLEN = 64 raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and siselect = 0x41, an attempt to access sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.

When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and the counter selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit in mcounteren = 0), an attempt to access sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.

If any extension upon which the underlying counter state depends for a given siselect and sireg* combination is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access the given state through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.
If the H extension is implemented, attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access vsiselect or vsireg* raise a virtual-instruction exception.
If the H extension is implemented, an attempt from VS-mode to access any sireg* (really vsireg*) raises a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg .CDE = 0.
If the H extension is implemented, an attempt from VS-mode to access any sireg* (really vsireg*) raises a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg .CDE = 1.
When attempted access to sctrdepth from VS-mode or VU-mode, a virtual-instruction exception is raised, unless CTR state enable access restrictions apply.
When CTR is active (current privilege mode enabled for recording and not frozen), qualified control transfers update the Entry Registers at logical entry 0.
When CTR is active, recorded transfers update the ctrsource .V bit to 1.

When CTR is active, qualified control transfers push older entries down the stack; the record previously in logical entry 0 moves to logical entry 1, the record in logical entry 1 moves to logical entry 2, and so on.
If the CTR buffer is full, the oldest recorded entry is lost.
When an SCTRCLR instruction is executed, all CTR Entry Registers are zeroed, and the CTR cycle counter and CCV are zeroed.
After SCTRCLR, any subsequent read of ctrsource, ctrtarget, or ctrdata that precedes the next qualified control transfer will return the value 0.
The first recorded transfer following SCTRCLR will have ctrdata .CCV=0.
When the optional x ctrctl .RASEMU bit is implemented and set to 1, indirect and direct calls are recorded as normal.
When x ctrctl .RASEMU is set to 1, function returns pop the most recent call by decrementing the WRPTR then invalidating the WRPTR entry (by setting ctrsource.V=0).
When x ctrctl .RASEMU is set to 1, co-routine swaps affect both a return and a call, overwriting logical entry 0 and not modifying WRPTR.
When x ctrctl .RASEMU is set to 1, other transfer types are inhibited.
When x ctrctl .RASEMU is set to 1, transfer type filtering bits and external trap enable bits are ignored.
When a trap occurs between enabled privilege modes, it is recorded as normal.
When a trap occurs from a disabled privilege mode to an enabled privilege mode, ctrsource .PC is 0.
When a trap occurs from an enabled mode to a disabled mode (external trap), it is not recorded by default.
When a trap return occurs between enabled privilege modes, it is recorded as normal, and ctrtarget .PC is 0.
When a trap return occurs from a disabled mode to an enabled mode, it is not recorded.
External trap recording depends on the external trap enable bits for the target mode and all intervening modes.
For records of external traps, ctrtarget .PC is 0.
If external trap recording is implemented, mctrctl .MTE and sctrctl .STE must be implemented, while vsctrctl .STE must be implemented if the H extension is implemented.

When an interrupt i traps to S-mode, it occurs if either the current privilege mode is S and SIE is set, or the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode, and bit i is set in both sip and sie.
Interrupts to S-mode take priority over any interrupts to lower privilege modes.
When reading or writing any implemented field of sip/sie, or writing any writable field of sip/sie, effects a read or write of the homonymous field of mip/mie.
